name: Globe and Mail cryptic crossword No 3,283

clue.text: What religious trainee is, and should have

definitions.note: read as what a trainee ought to have, split as two words

blocks.note: first meaning: a probationer in a religious order before taking vows
second meaning: split in two, the word says a trainee in holy orders should have no sin at all

explanation.surface: A reflection on what a young monk or nun is, and what they ought to possess.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half splits the answer as NO VICE: a religious trainee ought to have no vice.
explanation.definitionFit: A person newly entered in a convent or monastery, still on probation before vows, is called by this title.

indicators.note: things swimming move about freely, so the letters are set moving into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone reports a sighting of a monster swimming in a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: Swimming fits the loch monster story so well that it hides its job as the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Nessie is the popular nickname for the legendary creature said to live in Loch Ness in Scotland.

indicators.note: to check something is to hold it back or restrain it, so one piece holds another

blocks.note: one who checks is one who verifies
S is the standard abbreviation for society

explanation.surface: A fact-checker scrutinising a poet who belongs to high society.
explanation.walkthrough: Checker and checking look like a repeated idea, but the first is a noun giving letters and the second is the holding signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A versifier is someone who writes verse, a mildly dismissive synonym for a writer of poems.

blocks.note: C is the chemical symbol for carbon
a ream is a quantity of paper, 500 sheets

explanation.surface: Recommending the finest carbon paper for making copies.
explanation.walkthrough: Carbon paper reads as one old office item; split, it is a chemical symbol and a paper quantity.
explanation.definitionFit: The cream of something is its finest part, as cream rises to the top of milk.

blocks.note: first meaning: marks with cuts or lines, as a verb
second meaning: plural of a tally kept of points in a game, and also 'many' as in large numbers

explanation.surface: Complaining that a lot of vinyl records have scratches on them.
explanation.walkthrough: Records suggests vinyl discs with scratches, but it means tallies of points, and the answer also means many.
explanation.definitionFit: To score a surface is to cut lines into it, and scores are kept tallies of points in games.

clue.text: Harvester mainly scouring middle of field

indicators.note: mainly means for the most part, so most but not all of the word is kept
the middle of a word is its central letter, so only that one is taken

blocks.note: scouring an area is combing it; drop the final G
the central letter of a five-letter word

explanation.surface: A farm machine working its way through the middle of a field.
explanation.walkthrough: Combing an area means searching it thoroughly, so scouring gives COMBING, cut short to COMBIN, then the E from fiEld completes COMBINE.
explanation.definitionFit: A combine is the machine that reaps and threshes grain in one pass, short for combine harvester.

clue.text: Indian government on the up in Gujarat

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the following word rather than being clued by meaning
in a down entry, going up means reading from bottom to top, backwards

blocks.note: found inside the place name

explanation.surface: The Indian government is doing well in the state of Gujarat.
explanation.walkthrough: On the up sounds like prospering, but in a down clue it means read upward.
explanation.definitionFit: The Raj was British rule over India, and the word itself comes from the Hindi for reign or sovereignty.

indicators.note: in a down entry, one thing sitting on another comes above it, fixing the order

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
a broadcast is a programme, shortened
S again for second

explanation.surface: A second broadcast airing on another matter, like a repeat on a follow-up topic.
explanation.walkthrough: Issue looks like a topic or an edition; here it means offspring. Sprogs is British slang for children.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue in the legal sense means children or descendants, and sprogs is informal British slang for kids.

indicators.note: something done carelessly ends up jumbled, so the letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A careless officer puts a spanner in the works of the generator.
explanation.walkthrough: Warrant looks like a verb meaning justify, but warrant officer is a military rank.
explanation.definitionFit: A sergeant major is a senior non-commissioned rank, in the British Army a warrant officer appointment.

clue.text: Horror of headless man on horse

indicators.note: without a head means the opening letter is removed

blocks.note: a chess man is a piece such as a knight; lose its first letter
a mare is a female horse

explanation.surface: A gothic horror tale of a headless horseman, like Sleepy Hollow.
explanation.walkthrough: Man here is a chess man: the knight, with its silent K removed, followed by MARE.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightmare is a frightening dream, and more loosely any horrifying experience or ordeal.

clue.text: Briefly fool millions, in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: cut brief, a word loses its final letter

blocks.note: a fool is an idiot, with the last letter cut
M is the abbreviation for millions

explanation.surface: Deceiving millions of people for a short while, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: In a manner of speaking reads as a stock hedge phrase, but the last three words are the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom is a characteristic way of expressing things in a language or a fixed expression.

clue.text: Getting joke about setter in pub

indicators.note: about means around, so the first piece goes round everything that follows
one thing in another sits inside it

blocks.note: a gag is a joke
the setter refers to themselves as I
an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: Getting a joke about the puzzle setter while in the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest: the setter goes inside the pub first, and then the joke wraps round the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaining something means obtaining or acquiring it, a plain synonym for receiving or picking up.

blocks.note: someone at home is in
tuition is teaching or schooling

explanation.surface: Distrust of the practice of educating children at home.
explanation.walkthrough: Home schooling reads as one idea, but the two words give separate pieces; someone at home is said to be in.
explanation.definitionFit: A suspicion can be a hunch or gut feeling, which is what intuition gives you without evidence.

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into something, so one piece goes inside another
writhing means twisting about, so the letters are contorted into a new order

blocks.note: P is papa in the NATO phonetic alphabet
taken as written

explanation.surface: An irritable father barging in on a couple in a close embrace.
explanation.walkthrough: P goes into INTIMATE and the whole lot is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone testy is short-tempered and easily irritated, much like one lacking patience.

indicators.note: something new is remade, so the letters are formed afresh in a different order

blocks.note: taken as written
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A new king of Nepal who is more modest than his predecessor.
explanation.walkthrough: The R for king joins the fodder, and all seven letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain means simple and without show, so the comparative form means less showy or modest.

clue.text: Only question you after University Challenge’s conclusion

indicators.note: one thing after another follows it, which sets the order
a conclusion is an end, so only the closing letter is taken

blocks.note: uni is short for university
Q is the abbreviation for question
U stands for you in text speak
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: The single question you face once the TV quiz University Challenge has finished.
explanation.walkthrough: University Challenge is a long-running British TV quiz for student teams, but here the two words are split into separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Unique means being the single one of its kind, so it can stand for sole or singular.

clue.text: Oscar winner finally rebuked for bloomer

indicators.note: finally points to the end, so only the closing letter is kept

blocks.note: O is Oscar in the NATO phonetic alphabet
the final letter of the word
chid is an old past tense of chide, to rebuke

explanation.surface: An Academy Award winner told off for making a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: Bloomer means a blunder in British slang, which fits the scolding, but here it is something that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloomer is taken literally as a thing that blooms, and the orchid is a flowering plant.

clue.text: Northern Irish leaders start to anticipate everlasting peace

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, which alone is kept

blocks.note: N is short for northern
IR is an abbreviation for Irish
the van, or vanguard, is the leading part of an army
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Political leaders in Northern Ireland beginning to look forward to lasting peace.
explanation.walkthrough: Northern Irish leaders reads as one political group, but each word is its own piece; leaders are the vanguard, the troops at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: In Buddhism, nirvana is the final state of release from suffering, a perfect lasting peace and bliss.

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the words that follow rather than being clued by meaning

blocks.note: runs across the two words

explanation.surface: A burst water pipe somewhere in Cumbria, a county in north-west England.
explanation.walkthrough: Pipe suggests plumbing, but it is a tobacco pipe; the answer runs across cumBRIA Ruptured.
explanation.definitionFit: A briar is a tobacco pipe carved from the woody root of the tree heath.

clue.text: Hide microphone in the French horn

blocks.note: a bug is a concealed listening device
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Concealing a microphone inside a French horn.
explanation.walkthrough: French horn looks like one instrument, but French belongs with the, and horn alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A bugle is a simple brass horn without valves, used for military signals like reveille.

blocks.note: surface reading: speech that is rare or unusual
setter's reading: uncommon means not common, so refined standard speech, named after the monarch who reigned until September 2022

explanation.walkthrough: Uncommon means posh rather than rare, and the date points to Elizabeth II's death, after which the phrase became King's English.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names correct standard British speech, and its royal title changed with the monarch in 2022.

indicators.note: at regular intervals means every other letter is taken

blocks.note: second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: Often having to scold a naughty child.
explanation.walkthrough: Regularly reads as how often the child is scolded, but it tells you to take every other letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An elf can be used of a small, impish child, extending the sense of a mischievous little sprite.

clue.text: Elbow grease and energy for paper rounds

indicators.note: to round something is to go around it, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: E is the symbol for energy
the FT is the Financial Times newspaper
taken as written

explanation.surface: Hard work and energy needed for doing paper delivery rounds.
explanation.walkthrough: Paper rounds suggests a delivery job, but rounds is a verb: the newspaper goes round the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Elbow grease is an idiom for hard physical work, the exertion put into a task.

indicators.note: one thing after another follows it, which sets the order

blocks.note: per means each, as in ten dollars per person
to nod off is to drift into sleep

explanation.surface: Falling asleep after every drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay comes first in the clue but its pieces read in reverse order in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Pernod is a brand of French aniseed-flavoured spirit, an example of an alcoholic beverage.
